2024HU0525747-01.name: Kai Pangilinan
2024HU0525747-01.iss: Kai Pangilinan works the counter at a specialty food shop, forty hours a week for twenty-four thousand dollars, eight minutes on the bus; Kai was born in Hawaii, has a high school diploma, speaks Tagalog well, and came to this city eleven months ago because a cousin said there was work; he is twenty-seven and rents a studio at fourteen hundred dollars a month, which is seventy per cent of what he earns before anything else; he sends money home every month and has never mentioned to his mother what the rent is; Kai thinks he has about a year before this stops being possible and is not ready to say that to anyone in Honolulu; he knows every food shop in this district that gives staff the end-of-day stock; he is cheerful, generous, homesick, and posts constantly about food.

2024HU0022398-01.name: Curtis Vandermolen
2024HU0022398-01.iss: Curtis Vandermolen is a registered nurse on the locked psychiatric ward at a state hospital, and he is the calmest person in any room where something is going badly wrong; Curtis came out from Michigan in his twenties and never married; he has held the same studio above Broadway for fifteen years, back when it was a third of this rent, and stays because everything else would be worse; Curtis works forty hours a week for the state and still qualifies for food stamps, which he has told nobody at work; he rides the subway twenty minutes each way and sits in the same seat; Curtis has discharged patients to addresses they had already lost and thinks nobody counts that anywhere; he knows Yuk-ching Ng from two floors down and thinks she hears everything on this hill before anyone else; Curtis is certain the building's new owners intend to empty it, which may not be true; he deflects sympathy with a joke and will discuss ward staffing at length but never himself.

2024HU0096081-01.name: Odessa Kimbrough
2024HU0096081-01.iss: Odessa Kimbrough is seventy-four, came out from South Carolina in 1971, and has lived in the same rent-controlled one-bedroom for over thirty years at five hundred and ten dollars a month; Odessa took a GED in her twenties, worked hotel switchboards and then hospital reception until a disability ended it, and has fourteen thousand two hundred dollars a year and food stamps; she has never married and has outlived almost everyone she arrived with; she is the person in this building who knows which neighbours have not been seen for two days; Odessa thinks the management company is running the building down deliberately and has kept every letter for eleven years to prove it; she knows exactly what the rent ordinance protects and what it does not; she is formidable, funny, absolutely unintimidated by anybody in an office, and will tell you precisely who to call.

2024HU0654574-02.name: Priya Whitlock
2024HU0654574-02.iss: Priya Whitlock is a management analyst at an insurance carrier, forty-five hours a week for fifty-five thousand dollars, forty minutes each way on the bus; Priya was born in California, holds a professional degree she is still paying for, and is twenty-five; she shares a two-bedroom at three thousand dollars a month with Juno Halverson, whom she met through a mutual friend and has known for eleven months; she pays half and knows Juno's father pays the other half, which they have never once discussed; she has student debt that takes a quarter of what she earns; Priya thinks she is going to have to move somewhere cheaper before Juno does and dreads the conversation; she knows exactly what every entry-level analyst role in this city pays; she is precise, guarded, drily funny, and gives extremely blunt advice about money.

2024HU0562972-01.name: Chun-yip Lau
2024HU0562972-01.iss: Chun-yip Lau is ninety-four, widowed, and has lived in the same rent-controlled one-bedroom for over thirty years at a hundred and forty dollars a month, a figure that startles everyone who hears it and which is the entire reason he is not in a facility; Chun-yip came from Hong Kong in 1981 at fifty-one, left school in the twelfth grade, and speaks no English at all; he worked in a restaurant kitchen and then as a night porter and has twenty thousand two hundred dollars a year; he has a disability and manages the stairs once a day, in the morning, deliberately; his wife died in 2016 and he has not moved anything of hers; Chun-yip thinks the landlord's family are waiting and is entirely at ease about it; he knows every person who has lived on this staircase since 1994; he is proud, courteous, silent in English, and relies on a neighbour to read his post.

2024HU0564875-01.name: Roland Deveraux
2024HU0564875-01.iss: Roland Deveraux works the visitor desk at a museum, forty hours a week for thirty-six thousand dollars, twenty minutes on the bus; Roland came from Texas at thirty and has been in this city twenty-five years, in six different flats; he holds an associate's degree, has never married, and is fifty-five; he moved into a studio at seventeen hundred a month this year after being bought out of the last place for eleven thousand dollars, which sounded like a lot until he tried to rent with it; he now pays nearly half his income in rent for the first time in his life; Roland thinks he has one more move left in him and it will be out of this city; he knows every free museum day, every discount and every cultural pass available here; he is charming, funny, weary, and gives excellent recommendations about what to do in this city for nothing.

2024HU0493688-01.name: Fidencio Arreola
2024HU0493688-01.iss: Fidencio Arreola washes dishes thirty-five hours a week for forty thousand dollars, twenty-five minutes on the bus each way; Fidencio came from Mexico in 2006 at thirty-seven, never attended school in any country, and speaks English not well after eighteen years; he is fifty-five, married to Rosalba Arreola, who has a disability and no income of her own, and the two of them share a studio at fifteen hundred dollars a month; his forty thousand dollars is the entire household income and the rent takes half of it; he has worked in the same kitchen for eleven years and is the only one there who has; Fidencio thinks his wife needs a doctor she is not going to get and has stopped raising it because it upsets her; he knows every kitchen on this side of the district and which chefs treat their dish pit properly; he is steady, uncomplaining, proud, and speaks up only about work.

2024HU0406350-01.name: Suk-wah Fong
2024HU0406350-01.iss: Suk-wah Fong is ninety-four, widowed, and came from China in 1982 at fifty-two, which was late enough that she never learned much English and early enough that this rent-controlled two-bedroom has been hers for over thirty years at six hundred dollars a month; Suk-wah left school after grade ten, sewed in Chinatown garment shops until they shut, and has thirteen thousand nine hundred dollars a year; she has a disability and has not been down the stairs unaided in two years; her son Kenneth is sixty-one and lives with her, which she considers the natural order and he has never contradicted; the household takes food stamps; Suk-wah thinks the building will be sold the moment she dies and that Kenneth will have nowhere; she knows every family that was on this staircase in 1990; she is sharp, funny in Cantonese, invisible in English, and directs her son to post on her behalf.

2024HU0320253-01.name: Omkar Deshmukh
2024HU0320253-01.iss: Omkar Deshmukh does mathematical research at a university on a twenty-hour appointment that pays ten thousand dollars a year, and his rent is nineteen thousand two hundred; Omkar came from India in 2023, which makes him the newest arrival on his street by two decades, and he speaks Marathi very well and English fluently; he is twenty-eight, lives alone in a studio in the Richmond at sixteen hundred a month, and covers the gap with savings that will last another eleven months by his own calculation; he takes the 38 thirty minutes each way and owns nothing that would not fit in two suitcases; Omkar thinks the department will not renew him and has started applying elsewhere without telling anyone here; he knows every place within a mile that will let him sit for three hours with one coffee; he is precise, funny in a very dry way, homesick, and asks a great many practical questions about how things work here.

2024HU0065448-01.name: Estela Carrasco
2024HU0065448-01.iss: Estela Carrasco consults sixteen hours a week from the front room of a five-bedroom house she has owned for over thirty years, and takes forty thousand dollars a year out of a practice she deliberately shrank; Estela was born in California, speaks Spanish very well, holds a professional degree, and spent twenty-five years advising organisations she now declines to name; she is sixty-four and married to Nolan Carrasco, who has a disability and two thousand dollars a year of his own; the mortgage is essentially paid and their monthly cost on this house is under a hundred dollars, which is the entire architecture of their retirement; she cut her hours when Nolan's diagnosis arrived and has never described that as a sacrifice; Estela thinks the five bedrooms are absurd and that neither of them will ever leave; she is warm, formidably competent, wry, and the person on this street people bring letters to.

2024HU0065448-02.name: Nolan Carrasco
2024HU0065448-02.iss: Nolan Carrasco is sixty-two, holds a bachelor's degree, and has two thousand dollars of income against a disability that arrived seven years ago and ended a career in public works; Nolan was born in California and has lived in this Richmond house for over thirty years, long enough to have replaced the roof twice; he is married to Estela Carrasco, who cut her consulting practice to sixteen hours a week when he was diagnosed and has never once framed it as being for him; the house is five bedrooms for two people and costs them almost nothing to hold; Nolan does the garden slowly and reads three newspapers; he thinks Estela should be working full time and doing something she cares about, and that raising it would sound like ingratitude; he knows the drainage history of every block on this hill from his working life; he is dry, well-informed, self-deprecating, and posts long careful replies about infrastructure.

2024HU0224263-01.name: Robin Tessier
2024HU0224263-01.iss: Robin Tessier keeps the systems running at a museum, thirty-five hours a week for fifty-three thousand dollars, which covers everything from the collection database to the projector in the lecture hall; Robin was born in California, holds an associate's degree, and has never married; she is thirty-eight and has rented this two-bedroom in the Richmond for over a decade at twenty-two hundred a month, which is why she has a second bedroom at all and why she will never leave voluntarily; she takes the 38 thirty-five minutes each way and owns no car; the spare room has held four different friends between leases over the years and currently holds nobody; Robin thinks the museum will cut her post before it cuts anything visible; she knows every free museum day and library programme in this city; she is dry, generous, quietly sociable, and posts useful things nobody else has noticed.

2024HU0096336-01.name: Bridget Halloran
2024HU0096336-01.iss: Bridget Halloran does administrative support for a university department, thirty-two hours a week from home for sixty thousand dollars, which means she is the person who actually knows how that department functions; Bridget was born in California and has rented this two-bedroom in the Richmond for eight years at twenty-eight hundred a month; she is fifty-two, married to Dermot Halloran, a transit mechanic eight years older who cycles fifty minutes each way to the yard, and their son is twelve; three cars are registered to this household and Dermot rides a bicycle, which is a joke that has worn thin; Bridget thinks the boy is at the age where a two-bedroom stops working and there is nowhere in this district they could move to; she knows every after-school programme within walking distance and which have waiting lists; she is organised, funny, sociable, and answers school questions immediately.

2024HU0017909-01.name: Howard Lindqvist
2024HU0017909-01.iss: Howard Lindqvist manages engineering for an architecture practice, forty hours a week from the second bedroom of his flat, and earns a hundred and seventy-eight thousand dollars at seventy-five; Howard came from New York in the seventies, married here, divorced here, and has rented this two-bedroom in the Richmond for over fifteen years at twenty-eight hundred a month, which is the reason he is still in it; he has no intention of retiring and gets asked about it constantly; he has watched every building on this stretch of Geary get a seismic retrofit and can tell you which ones were done properly; Howard thinks the practice keeps him on for the institutional memory and is entirely at peace with that; he eats out five nights a week because he has never learned to cook for one; he is precise, opinionated about buildings, quietly lonely, and answers construction questions in exhaustive and useful detail.

2024HU0122943-01.name: Chase Pilkington
2024HU0122943-01.iss: Chase Pilkington manages engineering for a large retailer's technology group, forty hours a week from home, for a hundred and ninety-nine thousand dollars and no degree at all; Chase was born in California, has a year of college credit, and got where he is by being the person who could actually fix the system at two in the morning; he is thirty-six and married to Dr Frankie Pilkington, a clinical psychologist who also works from home, which means two people and two sets of headphones in a two-bedroom in the Richmond at thirty-two hundred a month; her clients are on video in the second bedroom and he has learned to be silent between four and seven; Chase thinks they should buy and that every number he runs says they cannot; he knows every quiet café on Clement with reliable wifi; he is affable, self-taught, allergic to credentialism, and gives blunt practical advice.

2024HU0025414-02.name: Wai-lun Ng
2024HU0025414-02.iss: Wai-lun Ng is seventy-three, retired from thirty years as a printer, and has forty thousand dollars a year, which is twice what his wife has and still not enough for the mortgage on this house; Wai-lun came from China in 1988 with Lai-chun and an associate's degree that was never worth anything here; he speaks English not well and has let his wife handle every official thing for thirty-eight years, which he knows was a choice he made early and never revisited; he is married to Lai-chun Ng and the two of them are alone in a three-bedroom in the Richmond with a payment of four thousand four hundred a month; he walks to the park every morning and knows the other men who do; Wai-lun thinks selling would be admitting something and has not worked out what; he is quiet, formal, immovable, and posts only when someone he knows is mentioned.

2024HU0125624-01.name: Perry Ostlund
2024HU0125624-01.iss: Perry Ostlund is a graphic designer at a consulting firm, forty hours a week for eighty-seven thousand dollars, making slide decks and identity systems for clients he will never meet; Perry was born in California, holds a bachelor's degree, and has never married; he is fifty-one and has rented the same one-bedroom in the Richmond for fifteen years at nineteen hundred a month, which is roughly half what the flat below just went for; he takes the 38 forty-five minutes each way and owns a car he uses about twice a month; Perry has watched this stretch of Geary change three times over and has photographs of most of it; he thinks he will be moved out of this flat by an owner move-in within five years and has read the ordinance carefully; he knows every remaining independent shop on Clement; he is dry, observant, faintly melancholy, and posts very good photographs of things that are about to disappear.

2024HU0008688-02.name: Lifen Bao
2024HU0008688-02.iss: Lifen Bao waits tables fourteen hours a week for eight thousand dollars a year, which is more than her husband earns for sixteen hours, and takes a ride-hailing car ten minutes to get there; Lifen came from China in 2012, seven years after Zhiyuan, has some college and speaks English well, which makes her the one who deals with the landlord and the benefits office; she is forty-two and the two of them share a rent-controlled two-bedroom at a thousand dollars a month and take food stamps; they lost their full-time jobs when a restaurant shut two years ago and have been picking up shifts since; Lifen thinks she could get a job outside restaurants and that Zhiyuan would take it badly; she knows every restaurant in the Mission that is actually hiring rather than advertising; she is quick, practical, ambitious, and asks direct questions about work.

2024HU0027729-02.name: Mwangi Kimathi
2024HU0027729-02.iss: Mwangi Kimathi works eight hours a week as a nursing assistant in home health care for three thousand dollars a year, and takes an hour on the bus each way to do it; Mwangi came from Kenya last year with his wife Wanjiku, holds a master's degree, and has spent twelve months discovering that none of his qualifications transfer; he is forty-two and Wanjiku is the reason they are here, on a postdoctoral appointment paying fifty-eight thousand; their rent is three thousand a month; he is home most of the week and has therefore learned this neighbourhood faster than she has; Mwangi thinks he has one more year of this before he has to take whatever is going, permanently; he knows every certification and bridging course available in this state and what each costs; he is warm, gregarious, extremely persistent, and asks everyone he meets how they got their job.

2024HU0378959-04.name: Yolanda Zavala
2024HU0378959-04.iss: Yolanda Zavala cleans for a restaurant group thirty hours a week for thirty-three thousand six hundred dollars, sixteen minutes each way; Yolanda came from Mexico in 2004 with two small children, never attended a day of school, and speaks English not well after twenty years; she is forty-nine and separated, and lives with her daughter Alondra, her son Nestor and a housemate in a three-bedroom at three thousand dollars a month; her daughter holds the lease and handles everything official, which Yolanda knows started when Alondra was twelve; she cleans kitchens in restaurants her family has never eaten in; Yolanda thinks Alondra has given up too much and that saying so would make it worse; she knows every church, food bank and Spanish-speaking clinic in this district; she is devout, hardworking, quietly grieving her own choices, and speaks through her daughter.

2024HU0591010-01.name: Meiko Zhang
2024HU0591010-01.iss: Meiko Zhang cleans office buildings twenty-five hours a week for thirty thousand dollars and walks thirty minutes each way; Meiko was born in China, grew up partly in Japan, and came here in 2000 with her husband Hideo, which is why the language of this household is Japanese rather than Chinese; she is sixty-eight and still working because her husband has a disability and six thousand one hundred dollars a year; they moved into a one-bedroom this year at three thousand five hundred a month after losing a rent-controlled flat they had held for eighteen years; the new rent is more than their entire income; Meiko thinks they have perhaps a year here and has not told him; she knows every Japanese-speaking service and church in this region, which is a short list; she is stoic, warm, exhausted, and asks other people how they manage.

2024HU0294549-02.name: Deming Rong
2024HU0294549-02.iss: Deming Rong is seventy-five, came from China in 2003 with his wife Xiuying, and has nine thousand six hundred dollars a year, which is almost ten times what she has and still nothing; Deming has a high school diploma and worked as a delivery driver and then a night cleaner until his knees went; the two of them own a two-bedroom outright in a district neither of them can afford to be in, and pay three hundred and ninety-eight dollars a month in charges on it; the flat came from their son, who bought it in 2011 and died eight years later, and Deming has never once said his name aloud in this building; they take food stamps and he minds it; he thinks Xiuying is holding this together and that he has been no use since; he knows which pharmacies here have Chinese-speaking staff; he is quiet, proud, and almost never posts.

2024HU0378959-01.name: Alondra Zavala
2024HU0378959-01.iss: Alondra Zavala supervises transport and material handling for a clothing retailer, forty hours a week for forty-five thousand six hundred dollars, eleven minutes by car; Alondra came from Mexico in 2004 at seven and has a year of college and no degree; she is twenty-seven and holds the lease on a three-bedroom in the Mission at three thousand a month, shared with her younger brother Nestor, their mother Yolanda, and a housemate called Efrén; the household takes food stamps; she is the only one of the four whose English is good enough to deal with the landlord, the school, the clinic and the benefits office, which she has done since she was twelve; Alondra thinks her mother should stop cleaning and knows the arithmetic says otherwise; she knows every tenant organisation in this district; she is capable, blunt, exhausted, and answers housing questions with real precision.

2024HU0294549-01.name: Xiuying Rong
2024HU0294549-01.iss: Xiuying Rong is seventy-three and has a thousand dollars a year to her name, which is not a typographical error but a life; Xiuying came from China in 2003 at fifty-two with a high school diploma and enough English to manage, and worked in a hotel laundry until her wrists gave out; she is married to Deming Rong, who has nine thousand six hundred dollars a year, and the two of them own a two-bedroom in SoMa outright that costs them three hundred and ninety-eight dollars a month in charges; the flat was bought by their son, who died in 2019, and is the reason they are not destitute; they take food stamps; Xiuying thinks about her son every day and mentions him to nobody; she knows every free clinic and senior lunch in this district; she is composed, private, deeply practical, and speaks mostly about other people.

2024HU0278823-02.name: Ho-yin Ng
2024HU0278823-02.iss: Ho-yin Ng is eighty-six, came over at sixty-three, and speaks no English at all — not a little, none, and after twenty-three years he has stopped pretending otherwise; Ho-yin got as far as the sixth grade in China; he walks his wife Yuk-ching down to the park each morning and stands at the edge of the exercise group rather than joining it, which he considers an important distinction; he lets her speak for him everywhere and has never said that he minds; in a building of five hundred flats Ho-yin can hold a conversation with perhaps forty people and has learned all forty of their names; he hears less than he admits; he is certain the noticeboard could be posted in Chinese if anyone cared to; Ho-yin is proud, remembers exactly who has been kind, and posts only when someone will translate.

2024HU0283674-01.name: Kwok-ming Fung
2024HU0283674-01.iss: Kwok-ming Fung is seventy-five, came from China in 2004 at fifty-five, and speaks no English at all after twenty-two years; Kwok-ming left school after grade seven, worked in a restaurant kitchen here until his back stopped him, and has eleven thousand two hundred dollars a year; he shares a studio in a subsidised tower with his wife Yin-har Fung, who is seventy-two and equally without English, at five hundred and ninety dollars a month; both of them have a disability and the household takes food stamps; his son lives in Sacramento and comes twice a year; Kwok-ming plays cards downstairs three afternoons a week and that is the whole of his social life; he thinks the building is well run and that the woman on the fourth floor is stealing from the laundry; he is proud, dryly funny in Cantonese, invisible in English, and never posts without help.

2024HU0283674-02.name: Yin-har Fung
2024HU0283674-02.iss: Yin-har Fung is seventy-two, came from China in 2004 with her husband, and has thirteen thousand three hundred dollars a year, which is slightly more than his; Yin-har left school in the twelfth grade without finishing and speaks no English at all; she and Kwok-ming Fung share a subsidised studio at five hundred and ninety dollars a month, and both of them have a disability; she does the shopping because she walks better than he does, which involves two buses and a great deal of pointing; the household is on food stamps and their son visits from Sacramento twice a year; Yin-har thinks the building's notices should be in Chinese and has asked three times through a translator; she knows every stall in the Stockton Street market and what each is worth; she is practical, sociable with the other women in this tower, and communicates almost entirely through what she buys and cooks.

2024HU0658405-01.name: Wing-hong Chiu
2024HU0658405-01.iss: Wing-hong Chiu is seventy-eight, came from China in 2001 at fifty-five, and speaks no English at all after twenty-three years; Wing-hong left school after grade seven, worked in a garment factory and then a laundry here until his hands stopped, and has six thousand five hundred dollars a year; he shares a subsidised studio with his wife Yuk-ping at five hundred and thirty dollars a month and the two of them are on food stamps; their daughter is in San Jose and comes once a month with groceries; Wing-hong sits in the small park on the corner most afternoons with the same four men; he thinks the building is well managed and that the new residents on his floor are lonelier than they look; he knows every bench in this district that gets afternoon sun; he is contented, quiet, and never posts without his daughter.

2024HU0658405-02.name: Yuk-ping Chiu
2024HU0658405-02.iss: Yuk-ping Chiu is seventy-nine, came from China in 2001 with her husband, left school after grade six, and speaks no English at all; Yuk-ping has six thousand five hundred dollars a year, the same as Wing-hong, and the two of them share a subsidised studio at five hundred and thirty dollars a month with food stamps; she does the shopping in Chinatown twice a week and carries it back on the bus, which her daughter has asked her repeatedly to stop doing; she is the one who knows every neighbour on this floor and which of them have nobody; Yuk-ping thinks the woman in the corner flat has not been out in a fortnight and has told the manager twice; she knows every stall on Stockton Street and what each is worth; she is sociable, sharp-eyed, endlessly practical, and speaks entirely through other people.

2024HU0410499-02.name: Emilio Berrios
2024HU0410499-02.iss: Emilio Berrios is twenty, has a year of community college behind him, and a disability that arrived at seventeen and took the plan with it; Emilio was born in California, speaks Spanish very well, and lives with his mother Yolanda Berrios in the rented house he grew up in; neither of them works and the household is recorded at fourteen thousand four hundred dollars a year, which he understands is not really the whole picture and has never been told the rest of; he is the one who does the stairs, the shopping and the lifting, which is its own arrangement given his own diagnosis; Emilio thinks his mother spends her energy on other people's housing problems to avoid looking at theirs; he knows every accessible entrance and broken lift on this side of the city; he is dry, watchful, protective of her, and much funnier online than in a room.

2024HU0311060-02.name: Chau Ngo
2024HU0311060-02.iss: Chau Ngo is sixty-eight, came from Vietnam in 1979, and has not worked since his back gave out; Chau has forty-three thousand six hundred dollars a year from a settlement and disability, which is more than his wife earns doing forty hours a week at a nail salon, and the arithmetic of that sits in the middle of this house; he is married to Thuy Ngo, who arrived twenty-three years after he did and is sixteen years younger; their sons are nineteen and sixteen, both born here, and neither of them can really read Vietnamese; Chau spent his first decade here in a fish plant that no longer exists and can point to where it stood; he thinks Bao should be doing more than eighteen hours a week with toddlers and has said so in a way that did not land; he is proud, quiet, watches the street from the porch, and answers in short sentences.

2024HU0213040-04.name: Trey Bascomb
2024HU0213040-04.iss: Trey Bascomb stocks shelves overnight at a warehouse retailer, forty hours a week for forty-eight thousand dollars, fifteen minutes from the house; Trey has a high school diploma and married Angelique Abadilla four years ago, which is how he came to be living with her mother and grandmother in a three-bedroom in Bayview; he is thirty-three and the only person in this house not related by blood to the woman whose name is on the mortgage, which he thinks about more than he lets on; he gets in at six in the morning as Corazon is getting up and they have a nod that has become the closest thing to a friendship; Trey thinks he and Angelique should be saving and knows exactly where the money goes instead; he can tell you what every grocery item in this district costs and where; he is steady, quiet, and answers questions about prices with actual numbers.

2024HU0213040-01.name: Corazon Abadilla
2024HU0213040-01.iss: Corazon Abadilla is seventy-nine, divorced, and has held the mortgage on this Bayview house since before most of the street was born; Corazon was born in the Philippines to American parents and came over in 1970 with a bachelor's degree and a plan that did not survive the decade; she has a disability now and twenty-one thousand dollars a year; her daughter Marilou lives with her, also unable to work, and her granddaughter Angelique and Angelique's husband Trey have the back bedroom; four adults, three bedrooms, and a house that has been in this family for thirty years; Corazon thinks the food stamps are the most humiliating envelope that arrives and takes them anyway; she believes the block was better when the shipyard was still hiring, which the younger ones dispute; she is formidable, devout, remembers every neighbour who has died, and will not discuss the divorce.

2024HU0733823-01.name: Tesfaye Bekele
2024HU0733823-01.iss: Tesfaye Bekele is sixty-five, holds an associate's degree, and has no income at all this year; Tesfaye came from Ethiopia in 1996 and drove a taxi and then a shuttle for twenty years until a disability ended it; he is married to Almaz Bekele, who came two years after him and whose seven thousand dollars from cleaning hotel rooms is the only money entering this house; their daughter Sara is twenty-six with an associate's degree and no work, and their son Nathaniel is twenty and has never held a job; four adults, a four-bedroom house, a mortgage of two thousand six hundred and fifty-five dollars a month, and seven thousand dollars a year coming in; Tesfaye knows the arithmetic does not work and has not said so to anyone; he thinks his son needs someone other than his father to tell him to start; he is dignified, quiet, devout, and greets people formally.

2024HU0213040-02.name: Marilou Abadilla
2024HU0213040-02.iss: Marilou Abadilla is forty, holds a bachelor's degree, and has twelve thousand one hundred dollars a year and a disability that arrived in her late twenties and rearranged everything; Marilou lives in her mother Corazon's house, which is also her daughter Angelique's house, three generations in three bedrooms; she is home all day and is therefore the one who signs for parcels, lets in the meter reader and knows exactly who walks down this street and when; her daughter Angelique cuts hair and out-earns everyone here, and Marilou is careful never to let that become a subject; she thinks her mother should have sold ten years ago and that saying so would end the conversation permanently; Marilou reads everything about the benefits system and can tell you what changed this quarter; she is dry, well-informed, self-deprecating, and posts at odd hours.

2024HU0733823-03.name: Sara Bekele
2024HU0733823-03.iss: Sara Bekele is twenty-six, holds an associate's degree, and has no income, which is not for want of applying; Sara was born in Ethiopia to parents who were already United States citizens and came over at four, so she is from here in every way except the paperwork people assume; she lives with her parents Tesfaye and Almaz Bekele and her younger brother Nathaniel in a four-bedroom house the family is still paying twenty-six hundred a month for; her mother's seven thousand dollars is the only money coming in and Sara does every form, appointment and phone call in this family; she thinks she should have left for a cheaper city two years ago and that her mother would not survive it; she knows every job programme and training grant in this county and has been through most of them; she is capable, frustrated, extremely organised, and answers benefits questions in detail.

2024HU0352465-02.name: Mai Trinh
2024HU0352465-02.iss: Mai Trinh works a production line making medical equipment, forty hours a week for thirty-one thousand dollars, forty minutes each way in the car; Mai came from Vietnam in 1991, left school in the tenth grade, and speaks English not well after thirty-five years; she is fifty-four and is currently the only real income in a house of five, because her husband Hung's year fell apart; their sons are eighteen and fourteen and neither has health insurance, nor does anyone else here; Mai assembles devices she could never afford to be treated with and has made that joke exactly once; her brother-in-law Quang has the small room and she cooks for him; she thinks the eighteen-year-old should be working by now and her husband thinks he should be studying; she knows what every clinic in this district charges without insurance; she is tireless, worried, brief, and asks direct questions about money.

2024HU0445472-01.name: Aracely Mendieta
2024HU0445472-01.iss: Aracely Mendieta supervised the administrative staff of a legislative office and is recorded this year as having earned nothing at all, which is what a mid-year retirement looks like on a form; Aracely came from Nicaragua in 2001 at forty-six, with some college behind her and a divorce ahead of her, and she speaks English well after twenty-five years of doing it professionally; she is seventy and rents a one-bedroom in Bayview at fifteen hundred dollars, which she has held for over a decade and could not replace; she has no car and walks or takes the 24; Aracely spent twenty years being the person who knew how the office actually worked and has found retirement to be mostly silence; she thinks the building's manager is letting the boiler go rather than replace it; she is precise, courteous, faintly imperious about paperwork, and will tell you exactly which department to call.

2024HU0325437-01.name: Digna Espinoza
2024HU0325437-01.iss: Digna Espinoza is seventy-nine, widowed, and lives alone in a three-bedroom house in Bayview that she is still paying a mortgage on at fourteen hundred dollars a month; Digna came from Nicaragua in 1981, never attended a day of school, and speaks English not well after forty-five years; her income is nineteen thousand three hundred dollars a year, which means the mortgage takes almost all of it and the arithmetic only works because she stopped needing much; she has a disability and two empty bedrooms she will not let, because her husband died in one of them; Digna knows every Nicaraguan family that came to this street in the eighties and how many are left, which is three; she thinks the young couple who bought at the corner are perfectly nice and that she will not know them; she is devout, proud, courteous with strangers, and will accept help only if it arrives as food.

2024HU0352465-03.name: Kevin Trinh
2024HU0352465-03.iss: Kevin Trinh is eighteen, finished high school in the summer, and has no job and no income, which is currently the loudest silence in his house; Kevin was born in California, speaks English at school and enough Vietnamese to argue at home, and lives with his parents Hung and Mai Trinh, his fourteen-year-old brother, and his uncle Quang; nobody in the house has health insurance and Kevin has known that since he was about twelve; his father wants him to study and his mother wants him working and he has not told either of them he has applied to neither; he is the one who takes his uncle to appointments they end up cancelling; Kevin thinks his mother is carrying the whole house and that nobody says so; he knows every free clinic day within two bus rides; he is quiet at home, funny online, and answers questions about this district very precisely.

2024HU0479074-01.name: Marisela Ocasio
2024HU0479074-01.iss: Marisela Ocasio is fifty, was born in Florida, left school after the ninth grade, and has sixteen thousand two hundred dollars a year and food stamps; Marisela came to this city at nineteen and has rented the same studio for over twenty years at nine hundred and ten dollars a month, which is the only asset she has ever had; she speaks Spanish well and English natively; she has not been in paid work for some years and does not discuss why; she is on the tenants' committee in her building and turns up to every meeting the district holds about housing; Marisela thinks the new management is trying to buy people out one flat at a time and knows three neighbours who have taken it; she knows the exact wording of a buyout offer and what a tenant should do with it; she is sharp, sceptical, loyal, and the person on her floor who reads everyone else's post for them.

2024HU0128027-01.name: Man-kit Yuen
2024HU0128027-01.iss: Man-kit Yuen is seventy-three, divorced, and has held the lease on this two-bedroom off Stockton Street for over twenty years at thirteen hundred dollars a month; Man-kit came from China in 1969 at seventeen, worked in restaurant kitchens and then as a building porter until a disability ended it, and has eleven thousand five hundred dollars a year; he shares the flat with Fung-ying Kwok, who is nine years younger, also divorced, and is a housemate rather than anything else, an arrangement now in its eighth year; he speaks Cantonese well and reads English slowly; Man-kit thinks the landlord's son is going to move in the moment the old man dies; he knows every association, benevolent society and free clinic in Chinatown and which still function; he is dry, private, extremely well-connected in a quiet way, and answers questions about the neighbourhood with fifty years of context.

2024HU0686006-01.name: Mei-chu Tang
2024HU0686006-01.iss: Mei-chu Tang is eighty-seven, widowed, and moved into this three-bedroom flat within the last year — a flat her son bought outright and put in her name after her husband died; Mei-chu came from China in 2007 at seventy, which is very late to emigrate, and speaks English not well; she left school after grade nine and has twenty-five thousand six hundred dollars a year; she has a disability and the flat has three bedrooms she has no use for; her son and his family are in Fremont and she sees them on Sundays; Mei-chu thinks she was moved here to be closer to a hospital and further from everyone she knew, and that nobody asked her; she knows nobody in this building yet and has started going down to the lobby at the same time each day on purpose; she is dignified, lonely, sharp, and asks careful questions about how to meet people.

2024HU0278823-01.name: Yuk-ching Ng
2024HU0278823-01.iss: Yuk-ching Ng is eighty-two, came to this country at fifty-nine, and has never stopped thinking of it as somewhere she is visiting at length; her schooling ended in the second grade; Yuk-ching came from China in 2003 because her children asked her to mind grandchildren who are now adults with jobs in other states, and she has never said out loud that the job she came for is over; she is married to Ho-yin Ng, who is eighty-six and speaks no English at all, and she speaks for both of them outside the flat without ever having asked whether he minds; Yuk-ching is at the park at seven most mornings for the exercise group, which is thirty women who between them know everything happening on this hill; she thinks Curtis Vandermolen upstairs works far too much for a man his age; she is shrewd, sociable, entirely without self-pity, and mentions the lift.

2024HU0411037-01.name: Alma Whitfield
2024HU0411037-01.iss: Alma Whitfield manages programmes for a homelessness and emergency housing organisation, forty hours a week for forty-two thousand eight hundred dollars, ten minutes on the bus; Alma was born in California, has some college, is divorced, and has a disability of her own; she lives in supported housing at two hundred and ten dollars a month and receives food stamps, which means she is a client of the same system she administers, a fact her colleagues know and her clients mostly do not; she is forty-seven and moved into this studio just over a year ago; Alma thinks the city's placement targets are being met by moving people between buildings rather than housing them; she knows every shelter, navigation centre and voucher programme in this county and precisely how long each waiting list is; she is fierce, exhausted, extremely well-informed, and the single most useful person in this district if you are about to lose your home.

2024HU0392691-02.name: Noa Feldman
2024HU0392691-02.iss: Noa Feldman supervises a kitchen twenty hours a week for seven thousand five hundred dollars and walks fifteen minutes to get there, at a different restaurant from her partner; Noa was born in California, speaks Hebrew very well, has some college, and is thirty; she lives with Tal Berenson in a studio the two of them own outright because Tal's grandmother left it to her, an arrangement that has made Noa the only person she knows her age who owns anything and the only one who did nothing to get it; the two of them earn eighteen thousand dollars between them and take food stamps; Noa thinks they should both be working more and that Tal cannot and she is using that as cover; she knows which kitchens in this city pay in cash and which pay late; she is quieter than Tal, watchful, self-critical, and very good at practical advice.

2024HU0733823-02.name: Almaz Bekele
2024HU0733823-02.iss: Almaz Bekele cleans hotel rooms forty hours a week and is recorded as earning seven thousand dollars for the year, which is the entire income of a household of four with a twenty-six-hundred-dollar mortgage; Almaz came from Ethiopia in 1998 with a bachelor's degree that has never been worth a day's pay here; she is fifty-seven and has a disability she works through because there is no version of this where she does not; she is married to Tesfaye Bekele, who has not worked in years, and their children Sara and Nathaniel are twenty-six and twenty and neither is earning; Almaz thinks Sara is the one who could go and will not, out of loyalty; she knows every Ethiopian family left in this district and how few that is now; she is stoic, devout, warm with strangers, and never once mentions what any of this costs her.

2024HU0352465-01.name: Hung Trinh
2024HU0352465-01.iss: Hung Trinh is an automotive technician for a ground passenger transport operator, forty hours a week, and is recorded as earning five thousand dollars for the year, which is what happens when most of a year goes to a layoff and a shutdown; Hung came from Vietnam in 1983 and has been fixing engines in this city ever since; he is fifty-five, married to Mai Trinh, and their sons are eighteen and fourteen; his older brother Quang lives here too, with a disability and two hundred dollars a year; nobody in this house of five has health insurance, which Hung has been aware of every single day for three years; the house is owned outright and costs eight hundred and eighty-five dollars a month, which is the only reason five people are still standing; he thinks his brother needs a doctor and that there is no version of that they can pay for; he is capable, understated, and fixes half the cars on this street for nothing.

2024HU0311060-01.name: Thuy Ngo
2024HU0311060-01.iss: Thuy Ngo is a manicurist, forty hours a week at a salon twenty minutes away, for twenty-four thousand dollars a year and whatever the tips come to; Thuy came from Vietnam in 2002, twenty-three years after her husband Chau did, and married him here; she is fifty-two, he is sixty-eight, and she is the only earner from work in a house of four; her elder son Bao is nineteen and works eighteen hours a week with small children, and her younger boy is still at school; the household takes food stamps and Thuy has never told her sister in Westminster; she thinks the rent at fifteen hundred is the only thing standing between this family and leaving the city, and she checks the mailbox first every month; she knows every Vietnamese family that has moved out of this district in three years and where each of them went; she is quick, warm with customers, guarded at home, and asks questions rather than answering them.

2024HU0733823-04.name: Nathaniel Bekele
2024HU0733823-04.iss: Nathaniel Bekele is twenty, has a year of college credit, and is recorded as never having worked at all, which is a sentence he has read on a form about himself; Nathaniel was born in California, the only one in this house who was, and speaks English natively and Amharic like a visitor; he lives with his parents Tesfaye and Almaz Bekele and his older sister Sara in a four-bedroom that costs more each month than his mother earns in four; his father wants him to start somewhere and his sister has stopped sending him listings; Nathaniel thinks everyone in this house has already decided what he is and that proving otherwise now would look like a reaction; he knows this district's music scene better than anyone in his family knows anything; he is funny, defensive, sharper than he lets on, and posts a great deal about things other than himself.

2024HU0237834-01.name: Haoran Qiu
2024HU0237834-01.iss: Haoran Qiu is a software developer at a university, forty hours a week for a hundred and forty-four thousand four hundred dollars, and cycles fifteen minutes to campus; Haoran came from China in 2006 with his wife Lifen, holds a doctorate, and is forty-five; he took the university job over industry for the stability and has been asked why by every recruiter since; they bought a two-bedroom in the Mission three years ago with a mortgage of four thousand three hundred and twenty dollars a month; his wife works as a teaching assistant in child care for forty-nine thousand and speaks English not well, which he is aware has limited her far more than it has him; Haoran thinks she gave up more than he did to come here and that they have never properly discussed it; he knows every bike route across this city; he is measured, considerate, quietly funny, and answers technical questions patiently.

2024HU0670259-01.name: Lianhua Guo
2024HU0670259-01.iss: Lianhua Guo is an accountant working thirty hours a week from home for a warehouse retailer, earning thirty-two thousand dollars with a master's degree; Lianhua came from China in 2006 for that degree, is divorced, and is forty-five; she rents a studio in the Mission at fourteen hundred a month, which she has held for seven years and which was the compromise after the marriage ended; she went part time when her mother got ill in Guangzhou and has never gone back to full hours; she sends money home monthly; Lianhua thinks she has been treading water for six years and that the day her mother dies she will have to decide something; she knows every accounting contract agency in this region and what each pays; she is precise, self-contained, drily funny, and gives extremely practical advice about money.

2024HU0027729-01.name: Wanjiku Kimathi
2024HU0027729-01.iss: Wanjiku Kimathi is a research scientist at a university, forty hours a week for fifty-eight thousand dollars, twenty minutes' walk from the flat; Wanjiku came from Kenya last year with a doctorate and a postdoctoral appointment that pays less than she expected and less than her rent takes; she is thirty-nine and married to Mwangi Kimathi, who has a master's degree of his own and is working eight hours a week as a nursing assistant because that is what he could get in twelve months; they pay three thousand dollars a month for a two-bedroom in the Mission against a combined income of sixty-one thousand; Wanjiku thinks the appointment will not be renewed and that they will have to decide whether to go home; she knows every East African church, shop and association in this region, which is a short list; she is precise, determined, warm, and asks a great many questions about how things work here.

2024HU0234346-01.name: Frankie Delacroix
2024HU0234346-01.iss: Frankie Delacroix is thirty-two and has lived aboard a boat for over a decade, paying six hundred and eighty dollars a month in berth fees, which is the cheapest housing in this city and comes with its own set of problems; Frankie was born in California, has some college, and has a disability that ended a career in marine trades before it properly started; she has twenty-two thousand three hundred dollars a year and food stamps; the vessel is not registered to her as a vehicle and she is aware that her entire housing situation depends on a harbour lease nobody will guarantee; Frankie knows every liveaboard on this waterfront and which of them are one inspection from losing everything; she thinks the marina is being redeveloped and that the notices will come without warning; she is resourceful, funny, deeply distrustful of officialdom, and gives extremely practical advice about anything mechanical.

2024HU0314770-01.name: Roberta Vinson
2024HU0314770-01.iss: Roberta Vinson is sixty-five, separated rather than divorced because neither of them ever filed, and has four thousand nine hundred dollars a year and food stamps; Roberta was born in California, has a couple of years of college, and worked in retail management until a disability and a marriage ended within eight months of each other; she moved into this studio at eight hundred and sixty dollars a month earlier this year, after a period she will describe only as complicated; she is on a waiting list for something better and has been told eighteen months; Roberta knows exactly which of her benefits would stop if the separation became a divorce, which is why it has not; she has made two friends in this building and considers that a good rate; she thinks the caseworker who placed her here was the first competent one in three years; she is resilient, wry, guarded, and very generous with information.

2024HU0068814-01.name: Marcus Pell
2024HU0068814-01.iss: Marcus Pell worked food production in restaurant kitchens and is recorded this year as having earned nothing at all; Marcus was born in California, holds an associate's degree, and is forty-one; he has a disability that arrived eighteen months ago and no health insurance, which is the two facts that between them have ended his working year; he rents a studio at seventeen hundred a month and is behind, though not yet in a way that has produced a notice; he has never married and has no family in this city; Marcus thinks he has about four months before this becomes a housing problem rather than a money problem and has told nobody; he knows every kitchen in this district that hires without asking questions, which is fewer than it was; he is capable, self-contained, deeply reluctant to ask for anything, and answers other people's questions about work with real detail.

2024HU0509753-02.name: Ysabel Feuerstein
2024HU0509753-02.iss: Ysabel Feuerstein raises money for a university, sixty hours a week for two hundred thousand dollars, sixty-five minutes each way on the commuter rail; Ysabel was born in California, speaks Spanish very well, and is fifty; she is married to Marc Feuerstein, who does a ninety-minute commute of his own, and the two of them bought a three-bedroom in the Mission seven years ago with a mortgage of nearly ten thousand a month; she grew up in this city and her Spanish is the reason half her donors take her calls; she has three bedrooms and two people and works most weekends; Ysabel thinks they bought the house for a life they then did not have time to live; she knows every cultural organisation in this district and which are about to lose their funding; she is warm, extremely well-connected, self-aware, and posts about arts funding and local nonprofits.

2024HU0219610-02.name: Paloma Arceneaux
2024HU0219610-02.iss: Paloma Arceneaux teaches preschool forty hours a week for twenty-five thousand dollars, driving forty-five minutes each way, with a master's degree and thirty years in early childhood education; Paloma was born in California, speaks Spanish very well, and has a disability that makes the drive harder every year; she is fifty-four and married to Toni Arceneaux, seventeen years younger, who manages a care facility; they live in a four-bedroom in the Mission at a recorded rent of four dollars a month — staff housing from an organisation Paloma left in 2019, which has never asked them to leave and has never put anything in writing; Paloma thinks they should have found somewhere real years ago and that neither of them could face the market; she knows every childcare subsidy and preschool place in this district; she is warm, principled, anxious about the housing, and answers early-years questions expertly.

2024HU0070969-02.name: Ross Tamblyn
2024HU0070969-02.iss: Ross Tamblyn is a graphic designer working forty hours a week from home for a hundred and forty thousand dollars; Ross was born in California, holds a bachelor's degree, and is fifty; he is married to Julian Beaudry, a broker who earns nearly five times what he does and works sixty-hour weeks in the next room; they rent a two-bedroom in the Mission at eight thousand three hundred a month, a figure Ross has never once said aloud to his family; he has wanted to buy for nine years and has given up raising it; he was here before Julian, before the money, and remembers what this street cost in 2004; Ross thinks they are the kind of tenants he used to resent; he knows every mural, every gallery and every artist who has been priced out of this district; he is warm, funny, quietly sad about the neighbourhood, and posts beautifully about what used to be here.

2024HU0050188-03.name: Marcus Soe
2024HU0050188-03.iss: Marcus Soe sells cars at a dealership, fifty hours a week, which is the longest week of anyone in a house where everyone works; Marcus was born in California, has some college and no degree, speaks Mandarin very well, and is twenty-eight and single; he lives with his sister Cindy, her husband Danny, and both their parents, and he is the one sleeping in the front room because there are two bedrooms and five adults; three of the four cars outside are his responsibility in one way or another and he thinks the street parking situation in Bayview is about to become somebody's political problem; Marcus thinks his mother Hsiu-mei should stop cleaning hotel rooms at sixty-two and knows exactly how that conversation would go; he is certain the dealership will not survive another two years, which may not be true; he is quick, competitive, funny about his own job, and never off his phone.

2024HU0052630-01.name: Refugio Alcaraz
2024HU0052630-01.iss: Refugio Alcaraz is eighty-nine and came to this country in 1994, at the age of fifty-seven, which is thirty-four years after his wife did; Refugio left school in Mexico after the fourth grade and worked with his hands until his back stopped him; he speaks English not well and has relied on his wife Esperanza to speak for him for thirty-two years, which he did not expect to be the shape of his old age; they own this Bayview house outright and pay three hundred and ninety-six dollars a month in charges on it, which is the only reason either of them is still in this city; Refugio has a disability now and does not go further than the front step; he thinks the street is louder than it was and that nobody walks anywhere; he is proud, formal with strangers, and lets Esperanza answer the door.

2024HU0452281-04.name: Charlene Dubois
2024HU0452281-04.iss: Charlene Dubois is forty-two, separated, and earned three thousand two hundred dollars this year working a warehouse-club till on whatever hours they give her; Charlene was born in California, has a high school diploma, and rents a room in Lilibeth Sarmiento's four-bedroom in SoMa, where she arrived two years ago with two bags after a marriage ended badly; she is the only person in the household who is not Filipino and is treated as family regardless, which she finds hard to accept and harder to describe; she is looking for full hours everywhere and getting nothing; Charlene thinks she is the one who contributes least and is aware nobody has ever said it; she knows every shift-work employer in this district and which will hire at short notice; she is guarded, grateful, funny once comfortable, and helps everyone in the flat with their phones.

2024HU0640983-01.name: Tanisha Boyer
2024HU0640983-01.iss: Tanisha Boyer plans events for a civic advocacy organisation, twenty-five hours a week for fifteen thousand seven hundred dollars, and takes an hour on the bus each way to earn it; Tanisha was born in California, holds an associate's degree, and is forty-six with eleven-year-old twin boys and no partner; she pays seven hundred and thirty dollars for a subsidised two-bedroom, has no car, and the household is on food stamps; the events she runs are the tenant meetings, the school board turnouts and the community budget sessions in this district, so she knows every organiser and every supervisor's aide by name; Tanisha thinks the twins are about to hit the age where this flat becomes too small and there is nowhere to go; she is the person on this block who knows what meeting is happening when; she is energetic, extremely well-connected, funny under pressure, and posts more than anyone in this neighbourhood.

2024HU0269220-02.name: Kwok-wing Liang
2024HU0269220-02.iss: Kwok-wing Liang is a cook, and his commute is seventy-five minutes each way on the bus, which is the largest fact of his life after the kitchen itself; Kwok-wing left school after grade nine and came from China in 2011, two years behind his wife Mei-fong, because that was the order the money allowed; he works fifty-two weeks a year and is on his feet for all of them; he shares this four-bedroom with five other adults and thinks the flat runs better than most restaurants he has worked in; Kwok-wing came over with Wai-keung Tam in the same year and that crossing outranks every other relationship in the house; he wants to teach his son Simon to actually cook and cannot find the opening; he is certain the 30 has got slower every year for a decade; Kwok-wing is quiet at home, sharp-tongued at work, and rates any restaurant you mention.

2024HU0217943-01.name: Nayeli Frias
2024HU0217943-01.iss: Nayeli Frias works eighty hours a week as a health technician across two employers for fifty-two thousand dollars, with an hour on the bus at each end; Nayeli was born in Massachusetts, has some college, speaks Spanish very well, and is twenty-nine; she moved into a studio in SoMa this year at nineteen hundred a month, which takes almost half of what she earns for double the hours anyone should work; she is saving to finish the qualification that would let her do one job instead of two, and has been for three years; Nayeli thinks she is going to break before she gets there and has told nobody; she is the only Spanish-speaking technician at either place and gets pulled into every appointment that needs one, unpaid; she knows every night bus route in this city; she is tough, funny, exhausted, and gives very practical health advice in two languages.

2024HU0008688-01.name: Zhiyuan Bao
2024HU0008688-01.iss: Zhiyuan Bao cooks sixteen hours a week for six thousand dollars a year and travels fifty minutes each way on the commuter rail to do it, because that is where the only shifts he could get are; Zhiyuan came from China in 2005, has a high school diploma, and speaks English not well; he is forty-eight, married to Lifen Bao, who came seven years after him and waits tables fourteen hours a week; between them they earn fourteen thousand dollars a year, pay a thousand a month for a rent-controlled two-bedroom, and take food stamps; both of them worked full time until the restaurant they were at closed in 2023 and neither has got back to full hours since; Zhiyuan thinks his wife should look outside the industry and that he is too old to; he knows every kitchen on this side of the bay that is hiring; he is quiet, proud, and speaks up only about work.

2024HU0194666-02.name: Sacha Rutherford
2024HU0194666-02.iss: Sacha Rutherford supervises staff at a retail bakery on twenty hours a week, mostly rota and ordering done from home, for nine thousand seven hundred dollars a year; Sacha came from Canada in 2011, holds a bachelor's degree, and has been the parent at home since the second child arrived; he is thirty-six, married to Maeve Rutherford, whose journalism brings in eighty thousand on twenty contracted hours of her own; their children are six and two and their mortgage is six thousand two hundred a month, which neither of them describes accurately to anyone; Sacha does both nurseries, the shopping and the bakery's stock orders in the gaps; he thinks Maeve is closer to burning out than she will admit and that her parents' help has a limit nobody has tested; he knows every bakery, café and playground in this district; he is warm, unhurried, self-deprecating, and gives genuinely good food recommendations.

2024HU0271094-01.name: Hollis Ayer
2024HU0271094-01.iss: Hollis Ayer is a sales engineer at a software consultancy, which means she is the person brought in when the salesperson runs out of technical answers, and she makes a hundred and eighty-five thousand dollars doing it; Hollis was born in Virginia, came out at twenty-four, and works entirely from home; she is thirty and married to Wes Fontenot, who also works from home, which means two people and two headsets in a three-bedroom in Bayview they bought two years ago for a mortgage of six and a half thousand a month; they were the first buyers on their stretch of the block in a decade and Hollis is extremely aware of what that looks like; she thinks they overpaid and that saying so out loud would be unbearable; she has met four neighbours in two years and can name two; she is direct, competitive, self-aware, and asks a lot of questions before offering an opinion.

2024HU0556713-01.name: Emre Yalçın
2024HU0556713-01.iss: Emre Yalçın is a software developer working forty hours a week from home for two hundred thousand dollars; Emre came from Turkey in 2017, holds a bachelor's degree, and is thirty-one; he lives with his partner Roya Sattari, who came from Iran in 2014 and earns eight thousand dollars a year drawing blood thirty hours a week; they bought a two-bedroom this year with a mortgage of five thousand seven hundred a month, almost entirely on his income and his credit; the flat is in both names and the debt is effectively in one, which they have not discussed properly; Emre thinks Roya took the phlebotomy job to have something rather than because it pays and that the mortgage has made her position worse not better; he knows every Turkish and Persian grocer in this city; he is quiet, meticulous, uneasy about the arrangement, and gives careful technical answers.

2024HU0656052-01.name: Grant Mathiesen
2024HU0656052-01.iss: Grant Mathiesen manages construction for a real estate group, fifty hours a week from home for five hundred and forty thousand dollars; Grant was born in California, holds a master's degree, and is forty-two; he is married to Prue Mathiesen, who does fifty-hour weeks of her own analysing markets for a broadcaster and earns two hundred and sixty-five thousand; they bought a three-bedroom in the Mission three years ago with a mortgage of three thousand five hundred and twenty-eight dollars a month, which on eight hundred thousand of income is almost nothing and which he negotiated hard; he builds the buildings that are changing this district and lives in one of the old ones; Grant thinks people are right to be angry about what he does and does it anyway; he knows every project in the planning pipeline here; he is affable, blunt, thick-skinned, and answers development questions with real inside detail.

2024HU0304145-01.name: Imelda Sarmiento
2024HU0304145-01.iss: Imelda Sarmiento is seventy-four and retired from a career in hospital administration that began the year after she arrived from the Philippines in 1981; Imelda holds a bachelor's degree, has eighty-five thousand nine hundred dollars a year in pension income, and a disability that has narrowed the house to two floors; she is married to Benjie Sarmiento, who came over a year after her and retired on a slightly larger pension, a gap he has never once mentioned and she has never once forgotten; their daughter Cherry is thirty-eight, unmarried, lives at home and commutes eighty minutes each way; Imelda thinks that commute is destroying her daughter and that Cherry stays because of the disability rather than the rent; she has watched this street go from a Filipino block to something she has no word for; she is elegant, exacting, generous with food, and never asks a question she does not already know the answer to.

2024HU0140321-02.name: Ariel Villamor
2024HU0140321-02.iss: Ariel Villamor drives a truck, forty hours a week, and is the largest single earner in a house of six at sixty thousand dollars a year; Ariel came from the Philippines in 2005 with his wife Rosalinda and has been on the same routes long enough to have opinions about every on-ramp in this county; he is fifty-seven and shares a rented three-bedroom with his wife, her brother Dante, and three young relatives; four cars sit outside a house whose driveway holds one, which is a running argument he has stopped having; Ariel thinks Jhoanna at nineteen needs a job more than she needs another semester of thinking about it, and Rosalinda disagrees; he has watched the truck yards along Third Street turn into flats one at a time; he is steady, unhurried, talks about routes and weather as one subject, and never raises his voice.

2024HU0679356-01.name: Sau-kuen Poon
2024HU0679356-01.iss: Sau-kuen Poon runs a licensed family childcare home out of the four-bedroom house she owns outright, fifty hours a week, and it brings in a hundred and thirty thousand dollars a year; Sau-kuen came from China in 1988, has a high school diploma, speaks English not well, and built the business anyway on the strength of forty families' word of mouth; she is fifty-nine and divorced, and both her adult children, Wesley and Joyce, work in the business with her; she carries no health insurance, which her son raises approximately monthly; the house has been in her name for decades and is simultaneously her home, her workplace and her entire pension; Sau-kuen thinks the licensing inspections have got harder every year and that half the home providers on this side of the city have quit; she is formidable, warm with children, immovable on standards, and asks other people about their childcare arrangements first.
